previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted for bilateral toe amputations due to dry gangrene, a complication from prior ICU stay and pressor use. She underwent uneventful amputation of three toes. Postoperatively, she developed fever and respiratory symptoms; chest imaging revealed a new left lung opacity, leading to a diagnosis of pneumonia. She was treated with levofloxacin, with clinical and radiographic improvement. Physical therapy cleared her for discharge home with home health services. She was discharged on postoperative day five in stable condition, with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and completion of antibiotic course. Follow-up was arranged with surgery and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with history of asthma, SCC of the lung s/p resection, 
chronic rhinosinusitis, A.Fib, and chronic pain syndrome (on 
chronic steroids and opiates) and with recent hospitalization 
for multiple R toe amputations in ___ (dry gangrene) 
who presents with worsening SOB, productive cough, and 
subjective fever at home.

#)  Cough/shortness of breath/hypoxemia: 
Initially felt to be concerning for pneumonia, so she was 
started on vancomycin and cefepime. Flu swab came back positive 
so she was started on Tamiflu. Then transferred to the floor.  
Antibiotics were discontinued soon after given lack of 
convincing evidence for pneumonia and several courses of 
outpatient antibiotics.  She improved and was weaned off 
supplemental O2.  She was provided with nebs for persistent 
wheezing and her prednisone was increased in the setting of 
increased bronchospasm.  She was given a short prednisone taper 
from 60mg x2d to 40mg x2d to 20mg (home dose), and then again 
40mg x2d to 30mg x2d to 20mg when it was felt her bronchospasm 
was not yet improved.  Wheezing decreased and she became 
subjectively better.  Finished 5 days of oseltamivir.

# Asthma: given standing and PRN nebs, and prednisone increased 
for several days as above.  

#) Leukocytosis: Baseline leukocytosis on chronic steroids, 
however acute on chronic elevation. This decreased with 
antibiotics, then continued to decrease even after antibiotics 
stopped.  When higher dose prednisone was restarted, white count 
again increased but never as high as her admission level.

#) HTN: Patient was hypertensive during time on floor thought 
possibly in part due to some element of fluid overload.  Her 
home carvedilol was continued and amlodipine 5mg daily was 
added.  
 
# Dry Gangrene/PVD: S/p 6 toe amputations during hospitalization 
in ___. Scheduled to f/u as outpatient with vascular in 
___. Vascular team examined wounds at bedside, and followed 
in house.  She was scheduled for an appointment with Vascular on 
discharge.

# Hyponatremia: The patient became mildly hyponatremic during 
her stay, likely secondary to fluid overload in the setting of 
increased steroids.  She was asymptomatic from this.  On the day 
of discharge patient refused to take extra dose of furosemide 
before discharge due to concerns about needing to urinate during 
transport home, but was instructed to take additional 20mg once 
home in addition to her regular home dose for one day.  She was 
ordered for electrolytes to be checked on ___ as follow up.

# CHF: Preserved EF on echo ___.  Maintained on home 
carvedilol and furosemide.

# AFib: Patient in sinus rhythm currently. Continued on 
carvedilol, clopidogrel (aspirin allergy), and Amiodarone.

# CKD: Near baseline throughout admission.

# Chronic Pain: Due to osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis 
per OMR. Status post multiple immunomodulatory agents (including 
methotrexate) and courses of steroids. Currently on chronic 
opiates.  No changes made to pain medications.
